title: Feeding your family well: labels, nutrients and plates

say: Feeding your family well: labels, nutrients and plates.
This is the video for Module 3 of Advanced Cooking and Nutrition: nutrition science for African families.
Good cooking feeds the body as well as pleasing the tongue. As the cook, you decide the salt, oil and sugar in the family pot.

say: Carbohydrates, proteins and fats give the body energy, measured in kilocalories. Carbohydrate gives 4 kcal per gram. Protein also gives 4.
Healthy adults need about 0.83 g of protein per kilogram of body weight each day.

Fat gives 9 kcal per gram, more than twice as much. One tablespoon of oil is about 120 kcal, so cutting two tablespoons from the family pot removes about 240 kcal. Measure your oil instead of pouring.
For example, Grace in Lagos checks a pack of instant noodles. The label says 45 g carbohydrate, 7 g protein and 14 g fat. These are illustrative figures, so always read your own label.

panel.heading: Reading a noodle label
items: Carbohydrate: 45 g × 4 = 180 kcal
Protein: 7 g × 4 = 28 kcal
Fat: 14 g × 9 = 126 kcal
Total: 334 kcal; about 38% from fat

say: Iron, vitamin A, iodine and zinc deficiencies are common, especially for women and young children. Vitamin C helps the body absorb iron from beans and greens, so serve an orange, pawpaw or guava with the meal.

panel.heading: Get more iron and vitamins from food
items: Eat an orange or pawpaw with beans
Drink tea between meals, not with them
Wash vegetables before cutting
Add leafy greens near the end; no potash
A little oil with vitamin A foods; iodised salt

say: Tea and coffee reduce iron absorption, so drink them between meals.

say: Use these targets for your 7-day plan. Adults need at least 400 g of fruit and vegetables a day. Yam and cassava do not count.
Less than 5 g of salt a day, just under one level teaspoon, and seasoning cubes count. Water instead of soft drinks.
For example, Blessing's family of five needs about 14 kg of fruit and vegetables a week, so she buys 7 kg twice a week.

panel.heading: Targets for your weekly plan
items: At least 400 g fruit and vegetables a day
Less than 5 g salt a day, cubes included
Free sugars under 10% of energy
A legume or animal protein every day
Cook once, eat twice

say: The healthy plate method: half the plate non-starchy vegetables, a quarter protein, and a quarter the starchy food.

panel.heading: Adapt the family pot
items: Half the plate: non-starchy vegetables
A quarter protein, a quarter starch
Measure the swallow with a small bowl
Cut salt and cubes gradually
Water or unsweetened zobo, not soft drinks

say: For many families the big change is the swallow. Measure the eba or pounded yam with a small bowl, and give more soup and vegetables instead.

say: For example, Joy in Calabar cut the salt in her soup from 3 teaspoons to 1.5, and the cubes from 4 to 1. She built flavour with stock, crayfish and iru instead, and cut down gradually so tastes could adjust.

say: Never stop or change a prescribed medicine because the diet is working, and do not use herbal mixtures sold as cures. Keep clinic appointments.

panel.heading: Food supports care; it does not replace it

cards.d: Never stop or change prescribed medicine because the diet improved. Ask the health worker.
Only on health worker advice. Too much iron poisons young children. Lock supplements away.
Constant tiredness, pale inner eyelids, poor sight in dim light: go to a health facility.

say: Do not give iron, vitamin A or other supplements on your own guesswork. Too much iron is poisonous to young children, and too much vitamin A is harmful, especially in pregnancy. Keep supplements locked away.

say: If someone is always tired, has pale inner eyelids, or sees poorly in dim light, take them to a health facility. Diagnosis belongs to health workers.

say: To remember. Fat carries more than twice the energy of carbs and protein. Eat vitamin C with plant iron. Aim for 400 g of fruit and vegetables and under 5 g of salt a day.
Use the healthy plate. And never change medicines through food.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Carbs and protein 4 kcal per gram; fat 9
Vitamin C with plant iron; tea between meals
400 g fruit and veg a day; under 5 g salt
Healthy plate: half veg, quarter protein, quarter starch
Never change medicines through food
